D: Two kids find a board game that unleashes the jungle on their town, and the man trapped inside it for decades.
P: Serve the snacks when the monkeys wreck the kitchen.
S: the monkeys tearing through the kitchen
Ripe bananas in thick slices dipped in a batter of flour, sparkling water and a pinch of sugar, fried at 180C until puffed and golden, rolled in cinnamon sugar.
everything comes charging through the house

Corn chips piled with cumin refried beans and melted cheese, baked bubbling, then loaded with tomato salsa, sour cream and pickled jalapenos. Spread 300g corn chips on a tray, spoon over 400g refried beans warmed with 1 tsp cumin and cover with 200g grated cheese. Bake at 200C for 10 minutes and top with 200g salsa, 150g sour cream and jalapenos. Serve straight from the tray while the cheese is still stretchy.
Giant pod pork and chive dumplings
the plants that take over the house

Pork and garlic chive dumplings steamed in a bamboo basket lined with cabbage leaves, with a soy, black vinegar and chilli oil dipping sauce. Mix 400g pork mince with a bunch of finely chopped garlic chives, grated ginger, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil and white pepper. Fill 30 round dumpling wrappers and pleat closed. Line a bamboo steamer with cabbage leaves and steam the dumplings over simmering water for 8 minutes. Mix 3 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp black vinegar and 1 tsp chilli oil for dipping.
M: Parrish house New England pot roast
the old Parrish house in a small New England town

Beef chuck seared and braised slowly with onion, carrot, celery, garlic and thyme in a rich tomato beef gravy, with potatoes cooked in the pot. Season a 1.5kg beef chuck roast and sear all over in a heavy pot. Remove, then soften an onion, 3 carrots, 2 celery sticks and 4 garlic cloves. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and 1 tbsp Worcestershire, add 750ml beef stock and thyme and return the beef. Cover and braise at 160C for 2 hours. Add 800g halved potatoes and cook 1 hour more. Slice and spoon over the gravy.
Van Pelt's juniper venison and redcurrant
the hunter who comes out of the game

Venison backstrap crusted with juniper, pepper and thyme, seared rare and sliced, with a glossy redcurrant and stock sauce and buttery parsnip mash. Crush 1 tsp juniper berries with 1 tsp pepper and thyme and rub over 800g venison backstrap. Sear in a hot pan 3 minutes a side for rare and rest 8 minutes. Add 250ml beef stock and 2 tbsp redcurrant jelly to the pan and reduce until glossy, then whisk in 20g butter. Boil 600g parsnips and 400g potatoes until soft and mash with 60g butter.
W: Brantford, New Hampshire in the fall

Soft, creamy fudge boiled from real maple syrup, brown sugar and cream, beaten until thick with toasted walnuts and cut into little squares. Boil 250ml maple syrup, 200g brown sugar, 150ml cream and 40g butter to 115C, stirring gently. Cool 10 minutes, then beat until thick and losing its gloss and stir in 60g toasted chopped walnuts. Spread in a lined 15cm tin, cool and cut into squares.
K: Brantford mulled apple and maple punch
a New Hampshire autumn in Brantford

Cloudy apple juice mulled with cinnamon, cloves, orange peel and a little maple syrup, served warm in mugs with a cinnamon stick. Alcohol-free. Warm 1L cloudy apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 3 strips orange peel and 2 tbsp maple syrup over low heat for 15 minutes without boiling. Strain into four mugs and add a fresh cinnamon stick and an orange slice to each.
